economy.summary: Introduced House Bill 1586 in 2025 to exempt overtime wages from Pennsylvania income tax, paired with a companion bill exempting tips, saying that allowing people to keep more of their earnings boosts the economy and helps workers who take extra shifts to stay afloat.
economy.short: Proposes exempting overtime wages and tips from state income tax.

taxes.summary: Voted against the 2026-27 state budget, saying Harrisburg has a spending problem rather than a revenue problem and that relying on one-time funds and accounting gimmicks for recurring expenses is reckless; he says the money should instead go to tax relief such as eliminating property or inheritance taxes and reducing gas taxes.
taxes.short: Voted against 2026-27 budget; proposes property, inheritance, gas tax relief.

abortion.summary: Voted no in December 2025 on House Bill 1957, a proposed constitutional amendment that would enshrine a right to abortion in the Pennsylvania Constitution, saying the state's existing law allowing abortion up to 24 weeks is already permissive and describing the amendment as devaluing life.
abortion.short: Voted against amendment enshrining abortion rights in state constitution.

education.summary: His official biography says he supports providing quality education opportunities for all students and notes he has served on the Basic Education Funding Commission; it does not detail specific education policies.
education.short: Says he supports quality education opportunities for all students.

energy.summary: Supported a November 2025 budget measure removing Pennsylvania from the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative (RGGI), calling the carbon-pricing program a major barrier to energy development and citing an estimated 22,000 direct energy jobs and nearly $8 billion in investment he says the state missed since joining.
energy.short: Supports Pennsylvania's exit from RGGI to expand energy development.

guns.summary: Voted against four gun bills in October 2025, including a red-flag law, expanded background checks for private long-gun sales, restrictions on firearm construction materials, and a ban on machine-gun conversion devices, saying the measures would not stop gun violence and would infringe on the rights of legal gun owners.
guns.short: Opposed red-flag, background-check, and other gun bills as infringing rights.
